findings.summary: The 'Reserve stock fails' saga step is a diagram node mixing the step name and its outcome, so the flow's failure branch is not visually distinct.
findings.evidence:
Reserve stock fails
local transaction
Refund payment
compensating action
findings.fix: Mark the failure as a separate branch (arrow labelled 'fails') leading to the compensating step.

findings.summary: The 'Consistency' bullet holds two ideas (saga plus eventual consistency, and avoiding 2PC).
findings.evidence: Consistency: saga plus eventual consistency, not distributed 2PC
findings.fix: Split into 'Use sagas with eventual consistency' and 'Avoid distributed 2PC'.

findings.summary: "Idempotent" is used as a requirement for consumers and for retries (page 4), but the chapter never defines it or shows why duplicates are harmless.
findings.evidence: "Consumer\nidempotent" and "Async downside? Duplicate delivery, so make consumers idempotent." Page 4 then says "Retry only idempotent calls".
findings.fix: On page 3, add a line such as "Idempotent: running the same request twice has the same effect as running it once (e.g. dedupe by message ID, or set status=paid instead of adding 10)". Page 4 can then refer back to it.

findings.summary: The availability row is not a verifiable comparison and the sync/async table mixes a formula with a vague word.
findings.evidence: Availability | Product of each service's | Independent
findings.fix: Write 'Availability | Multiplies across hops (3 x 99.9% ≈ 99.7%) | Each service independent'.

findings.summary: Interview Q&A on service discovery repeats the table above as prose, and the 'Async downside' answer drops the other cons.
findings.evidence: Client-side vs server-side discovery? Caller queries and balances itself; a proxy does it for the caller.
findings.fix: Drop the duplicate or add new content; keep the page focused on the visual comparison.

findings.summary: The sync vs async table's 'Con' cell for async lists three separate ideas in one cell.
findings.fix: Split into separate rows or short bullets.

findings.summary: Code snippet is shown without a one-line statement of its idea beforehand, and the timeout rule bullet is cryptic.
findings.fix: Put a one-line idea first (e.g. 'Separate connect and read timeouts') and then the snippet.

findings.summary: The 'Default is often infinite: one slow dependency eats all threads, outage cascades' bullet holds two ideas (cause and consequence).
findings.evidence: Default is often infinite: one slow dependency eats all threads, outage cascades
findings.fix: Split into 'Default timeout is often infinite' and 'A slow dependency eats all threads and the outage cascades'.

findings.summary: The circuit breaker diagram's last step 'Closed / probe ok' is ambiguous: the failure path from half-open back to open is missing, so the state cycle is incomplete.
findings.evidence:
Half-open
one probe call
Closed
probe ok
findings.fix: Show both outcomes from half-open: probe ok -> closed, probe fails -> open.

findings.summary: Timeout guidance is internally confusing: 'Caller timeout > callee timeout; total fits the user deadline' packs two rules in one bullet, and the 'Base it on p99' rule is not tied to it.
findings.evidence: Caller timeout > callee timeout; total fits the user deadline
findings.fix: Split into two bullets, one per rule.

findings.summary: The 'Big-bang rewrite' node in the migration section is an orphan label with no context, so it reads as an unexplained fragment.
findings.fix: Label it explicitly, e.g. 'Avoid: big-bang rewrite (all-or-nothing, high risk)'.

findings.summary: Fit-check table columns are not parallel: the last row mixes 'No CI/CD...' with 'Otherwise: modular monolith', which is not a condition when it pays off.
findings.evidence: No CI/CD, monitoring, tracing | Otherwise: modular monolith
findings.fix: Move 'modular monolith' into a separate takeaway line and put a real pay-off condition in that cell.

findings.summary: Check-yourself page poses questions with multi-idea answers, and the availability answer uses 99% while page 3 uses 99.9% with a different rounded figure, making it harder to compare.
findings.fix: Keep the numbers but note both are the same rule, or reuse the same per-service figure on both pages.
